cq_coverage.details: All competency questions are addressed by appropriate classes and properties. RoleAssignment pattern, InvoiceMessage structure, and data properties for identifiers, addresses, and invoice details enable direct answers to all CQs.

strengths: Rich and deep class hierarchy (3 levels)
Good use of restrictions for cardinality and role assignment
All classes and properties are annotated
Use of disjointness axioms for structural clarity
weaknesses: No General Class Axioms (GCAs) for advanced reasoning
No use of owl:equivalentClass for necessary and sufficient definitions
Disjoint unions could be added for Invoice sections

likely_oops_pitfalls: P7 (Missing domain/range for some properties if new ones are added)
P4 (Lack of equivalence axioms for advanced querying)

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce owl:equivalentClass axioms for classes like InvoiceMessage (e.g., define as a Message with header, detail, and summary).
Add General Class Axioms (GCAs) to capture complex business rules (e.g., 'Every InvoiceMessage with a Buyer RoleAssignment must have an Organization with a GLN identifier').
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables advanced validation and semantic inference

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Consider using DisjointUnion axioms for InvoiceHeader, InvoiceDetail, and InvoiceSummary to enforce partitioning.
Enrich Address with optional region/state and contact properties.

summary: The ontology is well-structured, covers all competency questions, and adheres to OWL 2 DL and best practices. Quality is high, with strong use of restrictions and annotations, though advanced axioms and equivalence definitions could further improve semantic rigor and reasoning support.
